name: Snuup — Get recommended by AI
author: menturi

sections.description:
Snuup does the work that gets a small business recommended by AI: it fixes your website so ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude and Perplexity can read it, writes new blog posts for it, and shows you what AI says about you. This plugin connects your WordPress website to your Snuup plan, so that work goes onto your website, by itself once you turn that on.

Once it’s connected:

  • Your new blog posts are published for you. Each blog post Snuup writes for you goes up as an ordinary WordPress post when you say OK, or on its day once you turn on auto-publish, and the pictures you added to it are saved into your media library. It opens in your editor like any post you wrote, and it stays yours, even if you cancel.
  • Your website fixes are made for you. Things like a robots.txt line that turns ChatGPT away, a homepage title that doesn’t say what you do, or a missing description. Each one is made when you say OK, or as soon as it’s found once you turn on auto-fix, and checked on your live website right after.
  • Bing hears about each new post. When a post goes up, Snuup tells IndexNow its address, so Bing, Yandex, Seznam, Naver and Yep can read it sooner. Google takes no such message.
  • You see your visitors from AI. The plugin counts the people ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude and Perplexity send to your website, and Snuup shows them to you.

You need a Snuup plan to connect: snuup.ai.

A post you change is never written over. If you edit a blog post Snuup published, your version stays. If you take a post off your website from your Snuup dashboard, it becomes a draft here, with everything in it kept.

External services

This plugin connects to Snuup (snuup.ai, run by Menturi OÜ). It is a connection to an external service and does nothing until you connect it. Once connected, Snuup also tells IndexNow (indexnow.org, run by Microsoft Bing with other search engines) the address of each blog post it publishes.

What is sent, and when:

  • When you click Connect to Snuup, the plugin sends the code you typed, this website’s address, the plugin’s version, what it can and can’t do on this website, the address where Snuup can ask it to check in, and its IndexNow key (see below), to the Snuup API at app.snuup.ai. Snuup answers with a key the plugin keeps.
  • Once connected, every hour the plugin checks in with Snuup (its version, what it can and can’t do, the WordPress version, its IndexNow key and whether another plugin here already uses IndexNow, and which of Snuup’s blog posts you changed, took off or put back in WordPress), asks for the work that is due (blog posts to publish, fixes to make, a post to take down) and says what became of each, with the post’s address.
  • When a blog post Snuup published goes up, changes or comes off your website, Snuup’s servers tell IndexNow (api.indexnow.org) so Bing, Yandex, Seznam, Naver and Yep can read it sooner. The message carries the post’s address, your website’s address and your IndexNow key, and nothing else. IndexNow takes it only from a website that shows the same key, so the plugin makes a key and serves it at /{key}.txt on your website. No file is written, and the plugin itself calls no search engine. If another plugin on your website already uses IndexNow (Rank Math, SEOPress, Yoast SEO Premium, All in One SEO, Microsoft’s IndexNow plugin), Snuup sends nothing.
  • When Snuup has work for your website, it asks the plugin to check in now, with a request to this website’s REST API (/wp-json/snuup/v1/wake) signed with the plugin’s key. The request carries nothing else, and the plugin turns away any request Snuup didn’t sign.
  • While your plan is on, every page of your website loads Snuup’s script from app.snuup.ai, the same one other websites use. For each visit it sends the page’s address and title, the website the visitor came from, the link’s utm_source, and whether they came from a Google ad. Snuup sees the visitor’s IP address, as with any request, and uses it only to stop counting the same visitor too often. It sets no cookies and keeps no IP addresses.
  • With the same hourly check-in the plugin sends the counts it kept of AI crawlers: for each day, how many times each AI crawler visited each page. No IP addresses are sent or kept.
  • When a blog post comes with pictures, the plugin downloads each one once from the address Snuup sends (on app.snuup.ai) into your media library, and the post shows it from there.
  • When you deactivate the plugin, it tells Snuup, so your Snuup dashboard shows it stopped.

When your Snuup plan ends, the plugin stops loading the script and counting, and picks up no more work. It keeps checking in, so it starts again if you do.

  • Service: https://snuup.ai
  • Terms of service: https://snuup.ai/terms

  • Privacy policy: https://snuup.ai/privacy

  • Service: https://www.indexnow.org

  • Terms of use: https://www.indexnow.org/terms
  • Privacy policy (Microsoft Bing, which runs api.indexnow.org): https://privacy.microsoft.com/privacystatement
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. Open Connect in your Snuup dashboard and copy your code.
  3. On the plugin’s page, paste the code and click Connect to Snuup.

Your Snuup dashboard shows it’s connected within a few seconds.
sections.faq:
What happens to my blog posts if I cancel or remove the plugin?

They stay. They are ordinary WordPress posts on your website, and their pictures are in your media library.

The fixes that changed a setting (in WordPress, Yoast or Rank Math) stay too. The fixes the plugin serves on each request (the robots.txt change, your homepage’s title and description, unhiding it from search, and the sitemap) last while the plugin is active, also after you cancel.

Does it change anything before I connect it?

No. Nothing changes on your website until you connect it, and only the work your Snuup plan sends after that.

I use Yoast or Rank Math. Do they conflict?

No. When Yoast or Rank Math runs, the plugin writes your homepage’s title and description into their own settings, so they keep printing them. Each new post’s title and description go into Yoast, Rank Math, All in One SEO, SEOPress or The SEO Framework the same way. With another SEO plugin, the plugin leaves your homepage’s title and description to it, and that fix stays open in your Snuup dashboard.

How are the fixes made?

Through WordPress’s own settings and filters, never by editing theme or server files. The robots.txt change goes through the robots_txt filter and takes out only the rule that keeps AI out: a bot you keep out yourself stays out. The noindex removal on your homepage goes through wp_robots, the homepage’s title through pre_get_document_title (or your SEO plugin’s setting), the description through wp_head, and the sitemap through wp_sitemaps_enabled. If WordPress’s “Discourage search engines from indexing this site” box is ticked, your whole website is hidden, so the robots.txt and noindex fixes untick it. Undoing the fix ticks it again. A change that doesn’t show on your live website is undone, and that fix stays open in your Snuup dashboard. The plugin never runs anything it downloads.

Fixes an earlier version made (schema code, llms.txt, redirects) keep working the same way: schema code is checked before it is printed, and a redirect can only lead to a page on your own website.

Will Google and Bing find my new posts faster?

Bing, Yandex, Seznam, Naver and Yep are told about each post the moment it goes up, through IndexNow. They decide when to read it. Google takes no such message and finds your posts its own way, through your sitemap and links. If Rank Math, SEOPress, Yoast SEO Premium, All in One SEO or Microsoft’s IndexNow plugin already tells IndexNow on your website, Snuup leaves it to them.

Does it work with a caching plugin?

Yes. Visits are counted by Snuup’s script on the page, which runs on cached pages too. After a fix, the plugin clears the common page caches before it checks your live website.

Does it work on multisite?

Each site connects on its own.
sections.changelog:
1.3.0

  • Bing, Yandex, Seznam, Naver and Yep hear about each blog post the moment it goes up, changes or comes off, through IndexNow. The plugin serves the key file IndexNow asks for; Snuup sends the message.
  • If another plugin on your website already uses IndexNow, Snuup sends nothing.

1.2.1

  • Your visits are counted on websites that use SiteGround’s Combine JavaScript setting. Before, it could stop Snuup’s script from counting them.

1.2.0

  • When there’s work, Snuup asks the plugin to check in, so posts and fixes go up within minutes, even on a quiet or cached website.
  • Fixes the plugin can’t make on your website are left to you from the start, with their steps. A change that doesn’t show on your live website is undone.
  • A post you change, trash or delete in WordPress stays that way, and your Snuup dashboard shows it. Saving a post without changing it doesn’t count, and a description you wrote stays yours.
  • Each new post’s title and description also go into All in One SEO, SEOPress and The SEO Framework.
  • A cover picture that didn’t download is tried again.
  • Snuup’s script counts your visits on every page, the same one other websites use.
  • The noindex fix removes the noindex tag from your homepage only. If WordPress’s “Discourage search engines” box hides your whole website, the fix unticks it too.
  • Deactivating the plugin tells Snuup, so you can connect it again right away.

1.1.0

  • New blog posts go up as WordPress posts. The pages published before stay pages and keep updating.
  • The pictures you add to a blog post are saved into your media library, so they stay if you cancel.
  • Nothing goes up until you say OK, or turn on auto-fix and auto-publish in Snuup.
  • Right after you connect, the plugin checks with Snuup a few more times, so what you say yes to goes up within minutes.

1.0.0

  • The plugin is now Snuup’s connection to your website: connect it with the code from your Snuup dashboard, and your new blog posts go up on their own, your fixes are made for you, and you see your visitors from AI.
  • Pages you change in WordPress are never written over.
  • The robots.txt fix takes out only the rule that keeps AI out. A bot you keep out yourself stays out.
  • The free check moved to snuup.ai.

0.4.1

  • The dashboard and this page now say what the service does today.

0.4.0

  • A report bought on snuup.ai connects to the dashboard with one click.

0.3.0

  • Redirect the dead pages AI links to, and publish a sitemap, with one click.

0.2.0

  • Apply the report’s fixes from your dashboard.

0.1.0

  • First release: run the free AI visibility check.
